text:
alex_cheng: Heads up — noticed a clear tail-latency regression on our INT8 KV path when mixed-precision kernel switching happens during small-batch interactive traffic. p99 jumped ~2.3x on canary yesterday around 03:12 UTC. :thinking_face:

maya_patel: Ugh. Is this the same cluster where we enabled opportunistic fp8 kernels?

alex_cheng: Yes. Canary had opportunistic FP8 decode + INT8 KV enabled. Baseline (INT8 kernels only) p99 ~180ms, mixed path p99 ~420ms on identical queries. p50 roughly unchanged.

jordan_s: Do you have profiler traces or a flamegraph?

alex_cheng: Pasted the relevant snippet from nvprof + runtime logs: 

```
# stack snapshot around affected decode
kv_load:int8 -> memcopy 14.2ms
kernel_switch_check 0.9ms
fp8_decode_kernel launch 0.6ms
kv_unpack_cast fp16 12.8ms
total decode step 48.9ms
NOTE: multiple memcopies when route chooses fp8 path for logits
```

alex_cheng: The weird bit is we see extra memcopy/unpack steps when the runtime decides to route to fp8 decode kernel mid-sequence — even though the cached KV is int8. So we do int8->fp16 cast+copy on hot path.

maya_patel: That matches hypothesis: opportunistic fp8 path assumes FP-friendly KV layout, so we force a conversion when formats mismatch. Conversion cost is small usually, but it becomes visible at small batch sizes because batching can't amortize kernel-launch overhead.

liam_o: Can you share p50/p95/p99 numbers and batch sizes from the A/B?

alex_cheng: Quick table from perf run: 
```
A: INT8-only, batch=1 => p50 42ms, p95 120ms, p99 180ms
B: mixed (opportunistic FP8), batch=1 => p50 44ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms
batch=8: A p99 60ms, B p99 62ms (effect gone)
```

jordan_s: So this is a small-batch tail latency issue. Kernel launch + memcopy + cast thrash. Does batching heuristic trigger kernel-switch checks per request?

alex_cheng: Yes — current heuristic checks compatibility per request and may decide to route to fp8 if recent sequence patterns show short decode-only steps. That check is cheap, but when it flips we pay heavy conversion cost.

perf-bot: ALERT: Compare run 2354319000 -> anomaly score 7.8 for kv_format_switch. Auto-attached profiling traces: /prof/2354319/kv-switch.

maya_patel: Two workstreams: (1) prevent format switch inside a single decode (sticky format per sequence), (2) fastpath conversion: avoid memcopy by casting in-place or using kernel that accepts int8 KV with fp8 logits. Thoughts?

liam_o: Sticky format sounds safest for correctness + tail latency. We could add short-lived hysteresis: once a sequence uses INT8 KV at step 0, pin to INT8 decode kernels for that entire request.

jordan_s: Hysteresis + add a metric so Optimize can recommend disabling opportunistic fp8 for low-batch interactive endpoints. Also consider changing batching heuristic to prefer coalescing small interactive requests into ephemeral micro-batches to amortize launch cost.

alex_cheng: I prototyped a sticky-flag patch (rk-2374) that prevents mid-sequence kernel flips. Local canary: p99 dropped from 420ms -> 190ms for batch=1, p50 unchanged. No correctness differences observed for our eval prompts so far.

maya_patel: Nice. Any memory/regression tradeoffs? Does sticky flag force us to keep both formats in memory?

alex_cheng: Good Q. Current patch keeps KV only in its stored format — no dual-copy. We avoid extra copies by preventing conversion at runtime. If we later want to change storage format we'd do an offline migration. So memory unchanged.

liam_o: What about INT8 quant calibration differences if we disallow opportunistic FP8? Could quality regress?

alex_cheng: Calib numbers: on eval set, int8-only BLEU/LL/perplexity delta vs fp8 is within noise for most models we serve. We already have per-model quality thresholds in model catalog; if a model shows degradation, we shouldn't enable int8-only. This is more of a deployment policy than a runtime thing.

jordan_s: Action items?

alex_cheng: Proposed plan: 
- Roll sticky-format patch to canary for interactive clusters (rk-2374) — owner: alex_cheng
- Add metric kv_format_switch_count and kv_format_switch_latency to console — owner: jordan_s
- Update batching heuristic: prefer ephemeral micro-batching when predicted concurrency low — owner: liam_o
- Add Optimize rule: "disable opportunistic fp8 for endpoints with median batch size <= 2" — owner: maya_patel

maya_patel: I'll open the Optimize rule PR and add guardrails. Also will add an evaluation job to run quality checks before flipping any per-model heuristics.

perf-bot: NOTE: scheduled perf regression sweep at 03:30 UTC to verify rk-2374 impact across model families.

liam_o: Cool. If rk-2374 passes, we should add telemetry to surface when conversions would have happened (to catch future regressions).

alex_cheng: Agreed. I'll attach the profiler traces and the small script used to reproduce locally: 
```
# reproduce (local canary env)
python tools/repro_kv_switch.py --model redwood-medium --batch 1 --mix-precision on
# output shows per-step kernel decisions
```

alex_cheng: TL;DR: tail-latency regression caused by mid-sequence format switches (int8 KV -> fp8 decode) at small batch sizes; sticky-format hysteresis fixes it without memory cost; next: canary roll + metrics + batching tweaks. :white_check_mark:

maya_patel: Thanks — I'll sync with Optimize next week and track the canary. :thumbsup:
